blocks.text:
After breakfast, take a guided tour with an English-speaking guide.

The route follows walkways along the cascades. The falls comprise 275 streams dropping approximately 60–80 m. The name Iguazu means “big water” in Guarani.

From the viewing platforms, you can see the calm river above the falls and the turbulent water below. Moisture hangs in the air, and rainbows appear above the gorge.

Optional visits are available to the Bird Park — USD 50 per person — or the Macuco Safari — USD 130 per person. The Macuco Safari includes about 3 km through the jungle in an open vehicle with a guide, a walk down to the river and a motorboat ride to the falls.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, cross the Tancredo Neves Bridge and visit the Argentine section of the national park with an English-speaking guide.

Here, the walkways run much closer to the water: above the river, alongside the cascades and by the Devil’s Throat. The roar of the water and the spray feel more intense than from the panoramic viewpoints on the Brazilian side.

After the tour, transfer to the airport, fly to Buenos Aires and transfer to your hotel.
